newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher on local demand.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher on local demand.

text.p: Argentine bonds were boosted by domestic demand from banks and brokers Thursday, as the market finished higher despite a sharp decline in U.S. Treasuries.
"There was strong local demand. Local banks have money to invest," said a trader at a local brokerage house. He said those local houses were speculating on future gains.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.40 to 122.70, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 advanced 1/2 to 87.

Traders said local players were betting Friday's U.S. November employment report could boost U.S. Treasuries and thus further underline the support lent to Argentine bonds in recent weeks from the U.S. market.
Analysts at Banco Frances said in an investor note that "the upward trend continues with firm prices and to levels which were nearly unexpected."
Separately, local bonds were helped by the placement by Argentina of 600 billion lire of 10-year bonds and 50 billion yen of samurai bonds due December 2002.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.48 percent from 6.75 percent.
